source.title: FiTS: Interpretable Spiking Neurons via Frequency Selectivity and Temporal Shaping

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies interpretable frequency and timing parameters in spiking neurons, but does not test whether neurons have one or a few human-named jobs, or evaluate held-out neuron explanations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports neuron-level frequency and group-delay organization and inference-time perturbations of target-frequency parameters. These concern a related parameter-level construct, not the claim versions' job counts, explanation tests, or attribution graphs. Benchmark accuracies and energy/runtime comparisons do not test the claim and are omitted.
record.test_reason: FiTS is a spiking-neuron design paper on auditory benchmarks. Its 'interpretable neuron-level summaries' are built-in frequency and group-delay parameters. It does not count how many jobs neurons have, test explanations against activations, audit polysemantic examples, or build neuron attribution graphs. It neither tests nor uses the claim. It does not even cite the essay, so 'cites_only' is the nearest fit and 'discusses' overstates the link. The relation is effectively unrelated (T6).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that FiTS improves feedforward SNNs over plain LIF on auditory benchmarks. Its learned target frequencies and group-delay shifts give parameter-level summaries of layer-dependent organization. The CT-to-DT analysis supports accurate interpretation in discrete time.
record.recipe_differences: The paper introduces and evaluates frequency-selective and temporal-shaping spiking neurons; it does not use the neuron-explanation or held-out scoring methods in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect of resetting target frequencies differs by hidden width; the authors report larger accuracy degradation at smaller widths. Learned frequency and group-delay patterns also differ between layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned target frequencies and group-delay shifts organize differently by layer. Shuffling neuron-to-frequency assignments drops SSC accuracy to near chance (about 3.5–4.2%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In FiTS spiking networks, explicit neuron-wise frequency parameters are layer-organized and tightly coupled to each neuron's learned weights.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 (stated in paper); provided venue metadata: arXiv.org
record.problems: The results are for spiking networks and measure frequency/timing parameters, not human-named neuron jobs or explanation accuracy. The Figure 2 organization results are qualitative in the text, with no numeric summary stated.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted benchmark accuracy, energy, runtime, and other ablation rows because they do not measure neuron jobs or held-out neuron explanations. Omitted CT-to-DT frequency alignment results because they assess frequency parameterization rather than the claim's construct.
record.verdict_notes: The word 'interpretable' here refers to designed neuron parameters in spiking networks, not to explaining what neurons do in trained ANNs or LLMs. No verdicts are given. The Table A.9 perturbation rows are ablations of the study's own method and could be dropped.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B pole audit and its shares of one-job, two-job, and not-understood poles.
Cross-model job shares, dense versus mixture-of-experts models, and scaling to trillions of parameters.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose as a shared feature, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
The proposed architecture, regularization, and tool explanations for messy neurons, and the estimates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
Attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons and reconstruction error.
Whether explanations based on activating examples predict where a neuron fires on separate activations.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.
